content: Fexinidazole and artemether/lumefantrine both prolong the QTc interval. Their concurrent use should be avoided, or alternative medications should be considered. Fexinidazole increases the levels or effects of artemether/lumefantrine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, which can lead to an increased risk of adverse effects. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Fingolimod and artemether/lumefantrine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid their concurrent use or consider alternative therapies. Artemether/lumefantrine increases the levels or effects of flecainide by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Fluconazole and artemether/lumefantrine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid their concurrent use or consider alternative therapies. Similarly, fluphenazine, formoterol, gemifloxacin, gilteritinib, givinostat, and glasdegib all share this QTc-prolonging effect with artemether/lumefantrine. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If coadministration is unavoidable, obtain ECGs at baseline, during treatment, and as clinically indicated. Discontinue treatment if the QTc interval exceeds 500 ms or if there is a change from baseline greater than 60 ms. Granisetron and artemether/lumefantrine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid their concurrent use or consider alternative therapies. Artemether/lumefantrine increases the levels or effects of haloperidol by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Haloperidol also prolongs the QTc interval, necessitating avoidance or alternative drug use. Histrelin increases the toxicity of artemether/lumefantrine by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate, hydroxyzine, idelalisib, and iloperidone also share this QTc-prolonging effect with artemether/lumefantrine. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Idelalisib, a strong CYP3A inhibitor, can further increase the levels of artemether/lumefantrine, necessitating caution. Imipramine and artemether/lumefantrine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid their concurrent use or consider alternative therapies. Artemether/lumefantrine increases the levels or effects of imipramine by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Similarly, inotuzumab, isoflurane, itraconazole, and ivosidenib all share this QTc-prolonging effect with artemether/lumefantrine. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If coadministration is unavoidable, monitor for QTc prolongation. Lithium and artemether/lumefantrine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid their concurrent use or consider alternative therapies. Artemether/lumefantrine increases the levels or effects of lofepramine by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Lofepramine also prolongs the QTc interval, necessitating avoidance or alternative drug use. Loperamide and artemether/lumefantrine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid their concurrent use or consider alternative therapies. Artemether/lumefantrine decreases the levels or effects of lovastatin by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is contraindicated. Macimorelin and artemether/lumefantrine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid their concurrent use or consider alternative therapies. Macimorelin increases the QTc interval by approximately 11 ms, which could increase the risk of torsades de pointes. Allow sufficient washout time of QT-prolonging drugs before administering macimorelin. Maprotiline and artemether/lumefantrine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid their concurrent use or consider alternative therapies. Artemether/lumefantrine increases the levels or effects of methamphetamine, metoprolol, and mexiletine by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Midostaurin and artemether/lumefantrine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid their concurrent use or consider alternative therapies. Mifepristone decreases the levels or effects of artemether/lumefantrine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Mirtazapine and artemether/lumefantrine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid their concurrent use or consider alternative therapies. Artemether/lumefantrine increases the levels or effects of morphine by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Moxifloxacin and artemether/lumefantrine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid their concurrent use or consider alternative therapies. Artemether/lumefantrine increases the levels or effects of nebivolol by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Nefazodone increases the levels or effects of artemether/lumefantrine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Nilotinib and artemether/lumefantrine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid their concurrent use or consider alternative therapies. Nortriptyline and artemether/lumefantrine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid their concurrent use or consider alternative therapies. Artemether/lumefantrine increases the levels or effects of nortriptyline by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Similarly, octreotide, olanzapine, ondansetron, and oxaliplatin all share this QTc-prolonging effect with artemether/lumefantrine. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Oxycodone and oxymorphone levels are increased by artemether/lumefantrine through CYP2D6 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Ozanimod and panobinostat both prolong the QTc interval when used with artemether/lumefantrine. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Panobinostat significantly prolongs the QT interval, and its prescribing information advises against use with QT-prolonging drugs. Pentobarbital decreases the levels or effects of artemether/lumefantrine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Strong CYP3A4 inducers can reduce serum concentrations of artemether/lumefantrine, leading to loss of antimalarial efficacy. Perphenazine, pimavanserin, ponesimod, prochlorperazine, promazine, and promethazine all prolong the QTc interval when used with artemether/lumefantrine. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Artemether/lumefantrine increases the levels or effects of propafenone and propranolol by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Protriptyline and artemether/lumefantrine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid their concurrent use or consider alternative therapies. Artemether/lumefantrine decreases the levels or effects of ranolazine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is contraindicated. Ribociclib and artemether/lumefantrine both prolong the QTc interval. Ribociclib decreases the levels or effects of artemether/lumefantrine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Romidepsin, selpercatinib, sertraline, and sevoflurane all prolong the QTc interval when used with artemether/lumefantrine. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Artemether/lumefantrine decreases the levels or effects of silodosin, simvastatin, and sirolimus by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. These interactions are contraindicated. Solifenacin, sunitinib, tacrolimus, tetrabenazine, thioridazine, timolol, and tolvatpan all prolong the QTc interval when used with artemether/lumefantrine. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Artemether/lumefantrine decreases the levels or effects of tolvatpan by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is contraindicated. Trazodone, trifluoperazine, trimipramine, and triptorelin all prolong the QTc interval when used with artemether/lumefantrine. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Artemether/lumefantrine increases the toxicity of umeclidinium bromide/vilanterol inhaled by prolonging the QTc interval. Exercise extreme caution when coadministering vilanterol with QTc-prolonging drugs, as adrenergic agonist effects on the cardiovascular system may be potentiated. Vandetanib and vemurafenib both prolong the QTc interval when used with artemether/lumefantrine. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Concomitant use of vemurafenib with QT-prolonging drugs is not recommended. Vorinostat and ziprasidone both prolong the QTc interval when used with artemether/lumefantrine. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Albuterol and artemether/lumefantrine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Artemether/lumefantrine decreases the levels or effects of almotriptan and alprazolam by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Artemether/lumefantrine increases the effects of amiodarone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Additive QTc prolongation effects may occur. Avoid concomitant use of lumefantrine with other QT-prolonging drugs, such as Class III antiarrhythmics. Artemether/lumefantrine increases the levels or effects of amphetamine by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Aprepitant increases the levels or effects of artemether/lumefantrine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Arformoterol and artemether/lumefantrine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Artemether/lumefantrine increases the levels or effects of aripiprazole by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism and decreases its levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Armodafinil decreases the levels or effects of artemether/lumefantrine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of artemether/lumefantrine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Artemether/lumefantrine increases the levels or effects of atomoxetine by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely.
